newsitem.title: CHINA: SILVER GRANT IN US$115 MLN BONDS ISSUE.
newsitem.headline: SILVER GRANT IN US$115 MLN BONDS ISSUE.

text.p: Silver Grant International Industries Ltd said on Monday it proposed to issue up to US$115 million guaranteed convertible bonds due 2004.
The bonds will carry rights to convert into Silver Grant shares at a conversion price of HK$5.52 per share subject to adjustment, the company said in a statement.
The bonds comprise US$100 million in bonds and an option to require the company to issue a further US$15 million bonds.
The bonds which will be issued at 100 percent of the principal amount, will bear interest at a rate of one percent per annum payable annually, it said.
The company said it had appointed ABN AMRO Bank N.V. and NM Rothschild & Sons Ltd to lead manage the issue which was to be offered to independent professional investors.
The bonds issue is subject to shareholders approval at an extraordinary general meeting on August 19, it said.
Application has been made to list the bonds on the Luxembourg stock exchange.

The net proceeds of the bonds of about US$96 million will be used to finance the company's investment in Beijing Wang Fu Jing Retail Management Co Ltd, in China Infra-Structure Investment Ltd, and for non-ferrous metals projects in China.
The balance of the proceeds will be used for general working capital, it said.
The issuer may redeem the bonds from August 23, 2000 to August 19, 2004, the company said.
Assuming full conversion of the bonds, the company will be required to issue 140.24 million new shares, representing 14.69 percent of its enlarged share capital, it said.
